topic: Points of interest within day-trip range of Apartments Napros, Sabunike

villa.name: Apartments Napros
villa.notes: Nominatim reverse geocodes the Google Maps coordinates to Put Kandelica, Sabunike, Privlaka 23233. The house number was not matched in OSM.

fieldNotes.distanceKmStraight: Straight-line distance from the house, computed from coordinates; it is NOT a driving distance.
fieldNotes.durationHours: Typical time on site, excluding travel; 0 means a practical stop.
fieldNotes.coordinates: WGS84, 5 decimals, from OSM (Overpass) unless the sources say Wikidata. For large parks the coordinate is an entrance or the centroid, as noted.

areas.name: Sabunike & villa
areas.description: The house, Sabunike centre (shops 150-200 m away) and the nearest bus stops.

areas.name: Nin & lagoon
areas.description: Nin old-town island, salt works, St Nicholas, Queen's Beach and the healing mud.

areas.name: Privlaka & Vir
areas.description: Privlaka village, the Vir bridge, Vir island and Kaštelina.

areas.name: Zadar old town
areas.description: Sea Organ, Greeting to the Sun, Forum, St Donatus, the cathedral and the Land Gate.

areas.name: Pag island
areas.description: The Pag Bridge and Fortica, Pag town, Kolan dairies, the Life on Mars trail, Novalja and Lun.

areas.name: Velebit & Paklenica
areas.description: Paklenica National Park entrances, Manita peć and the southern Velebit.

areas.name: Day-trip region
areas.description: All day trips: Krka, Plitvice, Kornati, Telašćica, Vransko Lake and Dalmaland.

items.name: Church of the Holy Cross (Nin)
items.description: A tiny 9th-century pre-Romanesque church in the middle of Nin old town, nicknamed "the smallest cathedral in the world" because it served the bishops of Nin. One art historian argues its deliberately uneven, elliptical plan was designed to follow the sun like a calendar.
items.whyGo: One of the oldest preserved churches in Croatia, 3 km from the house: an easy morning walk or bike ride with coffee in the old town after.
items.seasonality: Exterior viewable year-round; interior opening hours not verified
items.notes: Solstice/equinox light alignment is a widely repeated claim; only the 9th-century pre-Romanesque dating was confirmed in this research pass. [Verified 2026-10-16] Rewrote the solstice/equinox claim: Wikipedia presents the sun-tracking idea only as Mladen Pejaković's theory and does not mention solstices.

items.name: Church of St Nicholas on the mound (Prahulje)
items.description: A small Romanesque church from around 1100 that stands alone on a prehistoric burial mound in the Prahulje field between Nin and Zaton, with a lookout tower added when the Ottomans threatened the area. Tradition holds that Croatian kings presented themselves to the people here after being crowned.
items.whyGo: The most photogenic silhouette near Nin, especially at sunset. Flat farm roads make it an easy family bike loop from the house.
items.notes: The coronation story is tradition, not documented history. Do not use the Wikidata coordinate for Q16110052, which points at Pag; the OSM position is correct.

items.name: Statue of Gregory of Nin (Grgur Ninski)
items.description: A monumental statue in Nin of the 10th-century bishop Gregory of Nin, who defended the use of the Croatian language in church services. The best-known version of Ivan Meštrović's statue (1929) stands in Split; the Nin statue is near the Holy Cross church.
items.whyGo: A photo stop on the old-town walk that tells the story of why Nin matters to Croatian identity.
items.notes: OSM confirms a Grgur Ninski artwork in Nin. That it is a Meštrović cast was not confirmed by a Nin-specific source. [Verified 2026-10-16] OSM tags the Nin statue with artist:wikidata=Q313828 (Ivan Meštrović), but Wikipedia only says statues also stand in Nin and Varaždin without naming their sculptor. Keep 'Meštrović' out of copy until a Nin source confirms it.

items.name: Roman temple remains (Nin)
items.description: The foundations of a Roman temple of ancient Aenona, thought to date from the reign of Emperor Vespasian (1st century AD), on the northern edge of the old-town island.
items.whyGo: Shows that Nin was a Roman town long before it was a Croatian royal seat. Combine it with the Roman house remains a short walk east.
items.notes: The claim that it is the largest Roman temple on the Croatian/eastern Adriatic coast is often repeated but was NOT verified; do not use it in copy until it is confirmed.

items.name: Roman house remains (Nin)
items.description: The excavated remains of a Roman house on Nin's old-town island, mapped as an archaeological site.
items.whyGo: A short add-on to the Roman temple on the same walk around the island.
items.notes: Only OSM confirms it. Interpretation boards and access were not verified.

items.name: Nin old-town island, gates and bridges
items.description: A tiny walled town on an island about 500 m across in a shallow lagoon, reached on foot over stone bridges through the Lower Gate (Donja vrata) and the Upper Gate (Gornja vrata). Roman, early-Croatian and Venetian layers are packed into a few streets.
items.whyGo: The best evening stroll near the house, with ice cream, the lagoon and sunset light on Velebit.
items.notes: The island size is approximate. "Sunset light on Velebit" is a description of the view, not a sourced fact.

items.name: Museum of Nin Antiquities
items.description: A small archaeology museum in Nin old town. Its exhibits include Roman finds such as the hollow bricks (flues) once used to heat baths.
items.whyGo: A rainy-day or midday-heat option that explains the Roman and early-Croatian history behind the sights outside.
items.seasonality: OSM lists Mo-Su 09:00-22:00 (probably summer hours; unverified off-season)
items.notes: Opening hours, ticket price and operator (possibly the Archaeological Museum Zadar) were not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] Added the OSM opening_hours tag. The zaton.hr source calls it the 'Museum of Nin Antiquity'.

items.name: Church of St Vitus (Privlaka)
items.description: A small, fully preserved medieval church in Privlaka, described as dating from the 14th century. Mass is still held here in June for the feast of St Vitus.
items.whyGo: A quiet heritage stop 2 km from the house on the flat road towards Vir, and the patron-saint celebration of the village guests are staying in.
items.seasonality: Exterior year-round; feast-day mass in June (St Vitus, 15 June)
items.notes: Only a tourism listing gives the 14th-century date and the June mass, and the listing contradicts itself. Ask the Privlaka parish or tourist board to confirm.

items.name: Ruins of St Catherine's church (Sv. Kata)
items.description: The ruins of a medieval church dedicated to St Catherine, about 800 m from the house. Tourism sources group it with St Vitus as a 14th-century Privlaka church.
items.whyGo: The closest historic site to the house: a 10-minute walk for an early-morning or after-dinner stroll.
items.notes: The date comes from one tourism listing. Whether there is a path to the site and whether it is on private land was not verified; the owner should check.

items.name: Sea Organ (Morske orgulje)
items.description: Marble steps on the Zadar waterfront with tubes underneath that play chords as waves and boat wakes push air through them. Architect Nikola Bašić designed it, and it opened in 2005.
items.whyGo: The classic Zadar sunset: sit on the steps, listen to the sea and walk 20 m to the Greeting to the Sun.
items.notes: The architect and the 2005 opening come from general knowledge and the Wikipedia article; the summary fetched in this pass did not include them.

items.name: Greeting to the Sun (Pozdrav Suncu)
items.description: A circle 22 m across, made of 300 glass plates set into the waterfront paving, with solar panels underneath. After dark it puts on a light show, and smaller circles represent the planets.
items.whyGo: Kids run over it at dusk while adults watch the sunset. It is right next to the Sea Organ.
items.seasonality: Year-round; the light show runs after dark

items.name: Church of St Donatus
items.description: A massive round church begun in the 9th century by Bishop Donatus, built on the Roman forum and partly from its stones. It is Zadar's landmark building.
items.whyGo: The single most recognisable building in Zadar. You can see the Roman columns reused in its foundations.
items.seasonality: Exterior year-round; interior access and hours not verified

items.name: Roman Forum (Zadar)
items.description: The open square of the Roman forum of Iader, with paving, column fragments and a standing column, framed by St Donatus and the cathedral.
items.whyGo: You can sit on 2,000-year-old stones in the middle of the old town. It is free and always open.

items.name: Cathedral of St Anastasia and bell tower
items.description: The largest church in Dalmatia, a Romanesque cathedral whose bell tower is mapped as a viewpoint over the old town and the islands.
items.whyGo: The bell tower gives the best view in Zadar for orienting yourself on day one.
items.seasonality: Tower opening season and fees not verified

items.name: Land Gate (Kopnena vrata)
items.description: A Venetian Renaissance gate from 1537 carrying the winged lion of St Mark, the ceremonial land entrance to the walled old town.
items.whyGo: The best way into old Zadar if you park at the Foša harbour side, with the walls and the small Foša harbour right beside it.
items.notes: The 1537 date comes from Wikidata (inception). That the walls are part of the UNESCO "Venetian Works of Defence" listing is general knowledge and was not re-verified in this pass.

items.name: Five Wells Square (Trg pet bunara)
items.description: A square on the old-town ramparts built over a Venetian cistern, with five well-heads in a row and the Captain's Tower beside it.
items.whyGo: A shaded corner right inside the Land Gate. It works as a meeting point for groups exploring Zadar.
items.notes: The Venetian cistern detail comes from general knowledge and was not verified here.

items.name: Archaeological Museum Zadar
items.description: The main archaeology museum of northern Dalmatia, on the Forum, covering the Liburnian, Roman and early-Croatian periods.
items.whyGo: A strong option on a hot afternoon or a rainy shoulder-season day, and it gives the background to Nin's Roman and royal sites.
items.seasonality: Seasonal hours (OSM, checked 2025-09): Jun and Sep daily 09:00-20:00; Jul-Aug daily 09:00-21:00; Apr-May Mo-Sa 09:00-15:00; Oct Mo-Sa 09:00-17:00; Nov-Mar Mo-Fr 09:00-14:00, Sa 09:00-13:00
items.notes: [Verified 2026-10-16] The hours and website come from the OSM way tags (check_date 2025-09-13). The website resolves (HTTP 200).

items.name: Museum of Ancient Glass
items.description: A museum in a restored palace on the edge of the old town, devoted to Roman glass found in the Zadar region.
items.whyGo: A compact, air-conditioned museum that is easy to combine with Five Wells Square.
items.notes: [Verified 2026-10-16] The hours and website come from OSM node tags. The website resolves (HTTP 200).

items.name: Ljubač fortress ruins (Ljubljana)
items.description: The ruins of a medieval fortified town on a cliff above the sea at Cape Ljubljana, first mentioned as castrum Lubae in 1205 and linked by tradition to the Knights Templar. It overlooks the Ljubač bay and Pag island.
items.whyGo: A wild, unsigned 45-minute walk to a cliff-top ruin that few visitors find. Good for a sunrise hike or a retreat walking meeting.
items.seasonality: Year-round; avoid midday in Jul-Aug (no shade)
items.notes: There are no waymarks, so the page should link to a GPX track. "No shade" is an assumption about the karst terrain.

items.name: Roman harbour of Zaton (underwater)
items.description: A Roman-era port of the 1st-3rd century AD, discovered in the 1960s. It had a breakwater and a cargo wharf, now 1.5-4 m underwater after sea-level rise. Archaeologists found three Liburnian "sewn" boats (serilia) on its inner side.
items.whyGo: A rare story for culture-minded guests: a Roman harbour where boats were stitched together rather than nailed, a short ride from the house.
items.notes: The facts come from academic sources. The coordinates are a LOW-confidence guess in Zaton bay; the exact site is not mapped in OSM. Diving or snorkelling over protected archaeological sites may be restricted, so do not promote it as a snorkel spot without checking. There is no visitor centre.

items.name: Kaštelina fortress (Vir)
items.description: The ruins of a small Venetian fortress on the southeastern shore of Vir, thought to date from the early 17th century and built against raiders. Two towers survive, one of them carved with a winged lion.
items.whyGo: A coastal bike ride over the Vir bridge to a ruin at the water's edge, with a mud beach nearby.
items.notes: The OSM location is reliable. The date and the carving details come only from repeated, machine-translated Airbnb text (LOW confidence).

items.name: Fortica fortress at the Pag Bridge
items.description: A Venetian fortress from the 16th century on the southern tip of Pag, just below the Pag Bridge, built to guard the Ljubač strait.
items.whyGo: The classic photo of Pag's bare "moonscape" next to a turquoise strait. It is a short stop on any drive or cycling tour to Pag.

items.name: Pag Bridge (Paški most)
items.description: An arch bridge linking the mainland with the southern tip of Pag island over the Ljubač strait. It is the road (and bike) gateway to Pag from Sabunike.
items.whyGo: The views from the bridge and the parking areas at both ends show the bare white limestone of Pag that inspired the "Life on Mars" name.
items.seasonality: Year-round; can close in strong bora wind
items.notes: Bora closures are general knowledge for Croatian bridges and were not verified for this bridge. Cyclists should check the traffic and wind conditions on the bridge before going.

items.name: Our Lady of Zečevo (Gospa od Zečeva)
items.description: A pilgrimage church on the small islet of Zečevo, offshore north of Nin.
items.whyGo: A local pilgrimage tradition; the islet is visible from the beaches north of Nin.
items.notes: Only OSM confirms the church. The history (a 16th-century Marian apparition tradition) and the pilgrimage dates were NOT verified. Do not publish details until they are confirmed. [Verified 2026-10-16] Reverse geocoding places the islet in Općina Vrsi, not Nin, so the town field was corrected.

items.name: Paklenica National Park (Velika Paklenica entrance)
items.description: Two limestone gorges, Velika and Mala Paklenica, cutting into the southern Velebit above Starigrad. The park is known for big-wall climbing on Anića kuk and for well-marked hiking trails up to mountain huts.
items.whyGo: The best active day out from the house: hike or climb in the morning and swim in the sea at Starigrad in the afternoon.
items.notes: The second entrance (Mala Paklenica) is at 44.28308, 15.49281 (OSM way/592299039). The park's dog policy and ticket prices were not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] Removed the 'dog' tag: the park's site does not state its dog policy. The site confirms Entrance 1 Velika Paklenica and Entrance 2 Mala Paklenica.

items.name: Manita peć cave (Paklenica)
items.description: The park's only show cave, open to the public on guided visits, at 570 m above sea level above the Velika Paklenica gorge. It is about 1.5 hours' walk from the Velika Paklenica car park.
items.whyGo: It gives a Paklenica hike a goal that kids and teams remember.
items.seasonality: Guided opening in season; months not verified
items.notes: The opening months, the guided-visit times and the walking time from the entrance need checking on np-paklenica.hr. [Verified 2026-10-16] The OSM cave_entrance node 1312824946 sits at exactly the item coordinate. The 570 m altitude and the 1.5 h walk come from np-paklenica.hr. Opening months are still not published there.

items.name: Velebit Nature Park
items.description: Croatia's largest mountain range, 145 km long, which rises straight from the sea and forms the skyline seen from Sabunike. The nature park protects most of it, including two national parks.
items.whyGo: The mountain wall on the horizon east of the house, which turns pink in the evening light. Serious riders can use the pass roads for climbing days, and hikers can use the mountain trails.
items.notes: The coordinate is the park centroid from Wikidata, not a visitor point. Specific climbs to name (pass roads) still need to be researched. [Verified 2026-10-16] Corrected 'backdrop to every sunset': Velebit lies east/northeast of Sabunike, so the sun sets on the opposite side. The Wikidata centroid (44.483, 15.237) reverse-geocodes to Brušane on the Lika (inland) side, so it is fine as a map label but should not be used as a destination pin.

items.name: Life on Mars trail (Metajna, Pag)
items.description: A marked coastal trail near Metajna across bare, bora-scoured white limestone, linking the Ručica, Beritnica and Malin beaches, Slana bay and the Stogaj climbing rock. A trail race is held on 7, 15 and 25 km courses.
items.whyGo: The "Pag lunar landscape" experience: hike in the cool of the morning, then swim at Beritnica beach. Guided night hikes run from Ručica beach.
items.seasonality: Year-round; best Mar-May and Sep-Oct (almost no shade in summer)
items.notes: The Pag Tourist Board runs free guided summer walks ("moon walking") from late June to mid-September, according to secondary sources. [Verified 2026-10-16] Removed 'about 70 climbing routes': the official page says both that Stogaj has two 6 m routes and that it has 'nearly 70 marked routes', so the number is unreliable.

items.name: Via ferrata Life on Mars (Slana bay)
items.description: Opened in 2020 and described by the trail operator as the first via ferrata above the sea in Croatia: a 10-15 minute traverse 1-2 m over the water at Slana bay. It is reached by a marked 2 km trail from Ručica beach in Metajna.
items.whyGo: A short adrenaline add-on to the Life on Mars hike, suited to team-building groups.
items.notes: It requires a helmet, harness, lanyard with energy absorber and gloves. Where to rent the gear or book a guide was not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] The official page confirms the 2020 opening, the 10-15 min duration, the 1-2 m height and the mandatory gear. The 'Cape Sušac' endpoint was not on the official page, so it was dropped.

items.name: Veliko blato ornithological reserve (Pag)
items.description: A wetland on southern Pag that OSM maps as the Veliko Blato ornithological reserve, with a wooden bird-watching tower.
items.whyGo: A quiet spring and autumn stop for birders and cyclists on the southern Pag loop.
items.seasonality: Best in spring and autumn migration (assumed)
items.notes: Only an OSM viewpoint confirms it. The protection status, species and the best season were not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] OSM maps the wetland as 'Ornitološki rezervat Veliko Blato' (way 39916471, Povljana municipality), and the tower node is tagged fee=yes. The species and the best season are still unverified.

items.name: Lun olive gardens (Lunjski maslinici)
items.description: A protected grove of wild and cultivated olive trees at the northern tip of Pag, some of them estimated to be more than 1,000 years old, growing among dry-stone walls.
items.whyGo: The far end of a full Pag day trip: walk among ancient trees, then stop for cheese in Kolan on the way back.
items.seasonality: Year-round; the visitor centre season was not verified
items.notes: The age figure (over 1,000 years) is widely cited; confirm the exact wording on the official site. Lun is about 70 km and roughly 1h20 from the house (estimate).

items.name: Krka National Park (Lozovac entrance)
items.description: A river canyon of travertine waterfalls and lakes on the Krka, declared a national park in 1985. Boardwalks loop around the Skradinski buk falls.
items.whyGo: The essential waterfall day trip for families. Go early in the season or arrive at opening time.
items.notes: Swimming at Skradinski buk is banned (general knowledge, not re-verified). The drive is about 1h15 from the house (estimate).

items.name: Kornati National Park
items.description: A maze of bare stone islands and islets southwest of Zadar, usually visited on full-day boat trips from Zadar. Most trips also stop at Telašćica.
items.whyGo: A full day on the water with swim stops among stark white islands, for families and retreat groups who want to share a boat.
items.notes: The coordinate is the park centroid. Boats leave from Liburnska obala in Zadar (44.1140, 15.2295, approximate). Park entry fees are often not included in the trip price.

items.name: Telašćica Nature Park
items.description: A deep, sheltered bay on southern Dugi otok with sea cliffs on the open-sea side and an inland salt lake (Mir) where boat-trip guests swim.
items.whyGo: The calm-water swim stop on Kornati boat days, and the salt lake is warm early in the season.
items.notes: The coordinate is approximate (Wikidata). The salt lake name "Mir" comes from general knowledge; the source only says "Salt Lake". [Verified 2026-10-16] Replaced the coarse Wikidata point (43.9, 15.16) with the OSM nature-reserve centroid, about 2.2 km away.

items.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park (Entrance 2)
items.description: A UNESCO World Heritage chain of 16 terraced tufa lakes and waterfalls linked by wooden boardwalks, inscribed in 1979.
items.whyGo: The most famous nature sight in Croatia, a long but doable day trip (about 2 h each way by car, estimated). It is best in May-June or in October colours.
items.notes: The "16 lakes" count is general knowledge. Timed tickets may need booking in summer (not verified).

items.name: Vransko Lake Nature Park (Lake Vrana)
items.description: Croatia's largest natural lake (about 30 km² of water inside a 57 km² nature park) between Pirovac and Pakoštane. The park records 256 bird species, has been a Ramsar site since 2013 and has a 40 km bike trail around the lake.
items.whyGo: A top shoulder-season ride for cyclists and birders, and it is close to Dalmaland for families.
items.seasonality: Year-round; birding best in spring and autumn
items.notes: The coordinate is the lake centroid. The Crkvine entrance is about 2.5 km from Pakoštane (exact coordinates not mapped here). "Largest natural lake" is general knowledge. [Verified 2026-10-16] Corrected '260+' to 256 bird species (official page). Removed the 'e-bike hire at Crkvine' claim, which the official page does not support: it describes Crkvine as a camp. Moved the coordinate to the OSM lake centroid, about 600 m away.

items.name: Nin Saltworks (Solana Nin) and Salt Museum
items.description: Traditional salt pans in the Nin lagoon where sea salt and fleur de sel are still harvested by hand. The site has a small Salt House museum and a shop, and the fields can only be entered on guided tours.
items.whyGo: Watch the harvest and take home flower of salt. On summer open days the tours and the museum are free, and the Salt Festival is held in early August.
items.seasonality: Open days with free guided tours Jun-Sep (2026: about weekly, 5 Jun-10 Sep); the 2026 Salt Festival was on 30 Jul. The 2027 schedule is not yet published.
items.notes: The 2025 tour times were English 09:00, 11:00 and 17:00. Recheck each season. [Verified 2026-10-16] Official page checked: the 2025 tours were English at 09:00, 11:00 and 17:00 and Croatian at 08:00, 10:00 and 18:00, with no registration. The text says the festival is 'early August', but the 2026 table gives 30 July.

items.name: Gligora cheese dairy (Paški sir)
items.description: A family-run dairy in Kolan whose family has made Pag sheep's cheese (Paški sir) since 1918, according to visit-croatia.co.uk. Guided tours go underground into the maturing caves and end with a tasting in a room on top of the dairy with island views.
items.whyGo: The food highlight of a Pag day. Groups of more than 8 can pre-book, which suits retreats.
items.seasonality: From 20 Apr 2026: Mon-Sat 09:30-16:00, Sundays closed (official). The tour slot times are not listed on the official page.
items.notes: The page says "tours daily" but also "Sunday closed", so check whether Sunday tours run. Prices are deliberately omitted. [Verified 2026-10-16] Removed the unverified tour times (11:00-14:00) and 'cheese bar overlooking the Kolan plain'. The official page says Sunday is closed and that groups of more than 8 must pre-book by email. Prices are published but deliberately omitted. 'Since 1918' comes from one secondary source only.

items.name: MIH cheese dairy (Sirana MIH)
items.description: A second Pag cheese dairy in Kolan, close to Gligora.
items.whyGo: Lets cheese lovers compare two Paški sir producers in one stop.
items.notes: Visits and tastings were not verified.

items.name: Paška sirana (Pag cheese dairy)
items.description: A cheese producer near Pag town, mapped in OSM as a cheese shop.
items.whyGo: The nearest cheese stop on the way into Pag town.
items.notes: Shop hours and tastings were not verified.

items.name: Vina Otoka Paga (Pag island wines)
items.description: A winery on Pag mapped in OSM. Pag is known for its white Gegić grape.
items.whyGo: An island-wine stop on a Pag loop.
items.notes: Only OSM confirms it. The Gegić detail is general knowledge. Tastings and opening times were not verified.

items.name: OPG Mate Dušević olive oil (Ljubač)
items.description: A family olive-oil producer in Ljubač making monovarietal oils (Oblica, Drobnica, Levantinka, Leccino, Coratina) and a Selekcija blend. Olive Oil Times reports two NYIOOC gold awards, for Dušević Oblica and Selekcija.
items.whyGo: Award-winning local oil 11 km from the house. The producer offers oil tastings with a cellar tour, and pre-booked meals with wine for groups of 4 or more.
items.notes: Ljubač tasting experiences exist on Orioly, but it is NOT confirmed that this producer runs them. Ask the producer directly. [Verified 2026-10-16] The official site (Ljubač 83, 23248 Ražanac) confirms tastings and the cellar tour, so the earlier 'not confirmed' note is resolved. The NYIOOC award year is not stated in the source. The site's tasting prices are deliberately omitted.

items.name: Kraljevski vinogradi winery (Royal Vineyards)
items.description: A hilltop vineyard with a tasting room and restaurant above the sea near Petrčane, making Pošip, Plavac Mali and Crljenak.
items.whyGo: A sunset tasting with sea views, 8 km from the house: an easy group dinner venue for retreats.
items.notes: OSM tags it as a restaurant. Opening season and booking requirements were not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] The official site (HTTP 200) confirms Pošip, Plavac mali and Crljenak and a Konoba & Tasting Room at Ulica XIII br.10, Petrčane. It shows 'Closed' next to 1.11.2025, which suggests a seasonal winter closure.

items.name: Degarra winery
items.description: A Zadar winery (Put Vrela bb) that offers tastings. It is known for Bomary, a wine flavoured with Maraschino cherries and macerated herbs, alongside a Plavina rosé, the Bonterra red blend and a Maraština white.
items.whyGo: Easy to fit into a Zadar day, a short taxi ride from the old town.
items.seasonality: Official site: Mo-Sa 11:00-22:00 (OSM says Mo-Fr 08:00-16:00; confirm)
items.notes: [Verified 2026-10-16] Corrected the description of Bomary: the official site describes it as a Maraschino-cherry flavoured wine, not a blend. The 'former army barracks' setting and the 'first Zadar sparkling wine' claim come only from a chasingthedonkey blog, so they were dropped from the description.

items.name: Maraska shop (Maraschino liqueur)
items.description: A shop in Zadar old town for Maraschino, the cherry liqueur distilled from Dalmatian Marasca cherries that made Zadar famous.
items.whyGo: The classic edible souvenir from Zadar.
items.notes: [Verified 2026-10-16] Maraska's company site resolves. That this OSM shop node is an official Maraska outlet was not confirmed.

items.name: Benkovac Wine & Cycle (Ravni kotari wineries)
items.description: An event reported to be held each May, when Ravni kotari wineries around Benkovac open their doors to visitors on bikes. Nearby, the organic Škaulj winery in Nadin offers tastings by prior arrangement.
items.whyGo: A spring cycling and wine weekend that fits the cyclist audience well.
items.notes: The coordinate is Benkovac town (Wikidata). Event dates and whether the event still runs need confirming. [Verified 2026-10-16] Downgraded to low: the chasingthedonkey source does not mention the event at all, and the only description is one undated travel guide. Do not advertise it until the organiser confirms.

items.name: Zaton Holiday Resort pools and splash park
items.description: The big resort 3-4 km south of the house. Its pool complexes include a Forest Oasis zone with two water slides and a beachfront zone with a 304 m² spray park.
items.whyGo: Pools and slides close by for a beach-break day. The resort says its pool complexes are also open to external visitors.
items.notes: The resort's 2022 blog says the pools are for guests only, while a review mentions day visitors. Do NOT advertise this until day-pass access is confirmed. [Verified 2026-10-16] Upgraded to medium: the official pools page (now at /en/resort/pools; the old URL 301-redirects) states 'Our pool complexes are also open to external visitors'. The day-ticket price and the season are not published, so confirm them before advertising.

items.name: Adventure golf / mini golf (Zaton)
items.description: Mini-golf courses mapped next to the Zaton resort pools: an "Adventure golf" course, a felt golf course and a classic course.
items.whyGo: An evening activity for kids near the house.
items.notes: These are probably inside the resort; whether non-guests can play is not verified.

items.name: Nin Horse Centre (horse riding)
items.description: Trail rides suited to each rider's level, pony rides for children and beach rides, listed as part of the Zaton resort area.
items.whyGo: A gentle countryside or beach ride for kids and beginners, 3 km from the house.
items.notes: The OSM horse_riding node is unnamed. Matching it to this business is LOW confidence, and the listing may be out of date. [Verified 2026-10-16] Coordinates moved about 850 m to the In Your Pocket listing position (Dražnikova 76t, inside the Zaton Holiday Resort). The earlier unnamed OSM horse_riding node 1819150042 (44.23608, 15.16934) may be a different stable. The listing is undated, so confirm it still operates.

items.name: Adventure Park Zadar (ropes course)
items.description: Treetop rope courses 1-10 m high with ziplines (the longest 50 m) in the pines at Kožino, plus bouldering, paintball and quad off-road tours. It has been open since 2013, with a second park in Biograd.
items.whyGo: A shaded half-day for active kids and a classic team-building option for retreats.
items.seasonality: Official site says 'open on call': book ahead. Minimum height 120 cm for the ropes.
items.notes: Season, hours and age limits need checking on the official site. [Verified 2026-10-16] Confirmed on the official site (Kožinska cesta 108).

items.name: Dalmaland Fun Park and Aquapark
items.description: A theme park with rides and themed worlds (pirate city, space, Wild West) plus a water park that opened in July 2023.
items.whyGo: The big day out for kids, combinable with Vransko Lake.
items.seasonality: Fun park from late Apr to late Sep; aquapark Jul-Aug plus a September post-season (varies by year)
items.notes: There is no "Dinopark" near Zadar; the nearest dinosaur-themed attraction is the section in this fun park. The aquapark is mapped at 43.93058, 15.48. About 55 minutes by car (estimate).

items.name: Moon Fun Park (trampoline park, Zadar)
items.description: A kids' entertainment centre in Zadar (Splitska ulica 3, per OSM) with a trampoline park, VR arena, sim-racing simulators and mini golf.
items.whyGo: A rainy-day or too-hot-day option for kids.
items.seasonality: Official site: Mon closed; Tue-Thu and Sun 15:30-22:00; Fri-Sat 15:30-23:00 (differs from OSM)
items.notes: Only OSM confirms it. The website, opening times and whether it is indoors were not verified. [Verified 2026-10-16] The official site confirms the attractions. It does not say whether the venue is indoors, and it mentions closures in severe storms, so do not market it as a rainy-day option yet.

items.name: Sabunike
items.description: The house's hamlet, a quiet strip of holiday homes on a shallow sandy bay facing Velebit, part of Privlaka municipality. Its centre has a small supermarket, a bakery, a fish shop, market stalls and an ATM within 200 m of the house.
items.whyGo: Everything for a slow morning is a 3-minute walk away.
items.notes: A reverse geocode confirms the house coordinates (44.25871, 15.15892) are on Put Kandelica, Sabunike, Privlaka 23233. Shop seasonality is not verified.

items.name: Nin
items.description: A former Croatian royal and episcopal seat on a lagoon island, 3 km from the house. It has salt pans, sandy beaches and healing mud.
items.whyGo: Your nearest "real" town: shops, restaurants, history and the long sandy beaches, all within cycling distance.

items.name: Privlaka
items.description: The fishing and farming village (one municipality, about 2,250 people in 2011) that Sabunike belongs to, on the narrow neck of land facing Vir.
items.whyGo: The post office, a pharmacy, supermarkets and a fish shop, 3-4 km from the house.

items.name: Vir (island)
items.description: A low, flat island joined to Privlaka by a bridge, first mentioned in 1069. It has holiday-home villages, beaches and a lighthouse on its western tip.
items.whyGo: A flat, easy cycling island close to the house, with the Kaštelina ruins and beach bars.
items.notes: The lighthouse is general knowledge and was not verified in this pass.

items.name: Zadar
items.description: The oldest continuously inhabited city in Croatia and the regional capital: a walled peninsula old town with Roman, medieval and Venetian layers and the Sea Organ waterfront. It is about 20 km and roughly 25 minutes by car from the house (estimate).
items.whyGo: The cultural day trip and the airport city. Evenings on the Riva with the Sea Organ are the highlight.

items.name: Pag (town)
items.description: A compact 15th-century planned town on the bay of Pag island, known for Pag lace, cheese and salt.
items.whyGo: The centre of a Pag island loop: the bridge, Fortica, Pag town, then cheese in Kolan.
items.notes: The 15th-century planned-town and Pag lace claims are general knowledge and were not verified in this pass.

items.name: Novalja and Zrće beach
items.description: The main resort town of northern Pag. Nearby Zrće is a long pebble beach famous for its summer club festivals, and it has held Blue Flag status (first awarded in 2003).
items.whyGo: Nightlife for groups and young adults, and the base for the Life on Mars trail at Metajna.
items.seasonality: Clubs at Zrće mainly Jun-Sep (not verified)
items.notes: [Verified 2026-10-16] Wikipedia gives the Blue Flag award year as 2003; current-year Blue Flag status was not re-verified.

items.notes: OSM has no opening hours; it is probably seasonal. Ask the owner.

Our Lady of Zečevo: history and pilgrimage dates; how to get to the islet.
Nin salt works 2026/2027 open-day schedule and tour times.

OPG Dušević: which year were the NYIOOC gold awards? Tastings are confirmed on the official site.
Opening seasons/hours for: Museum of Nin Antiquities, Zadar museums, Kraljevski vinogradi, Adventure Park Zadar, Moon Fun Park.
Benkovac Wine & Cycle: next date and whether still held.
Recommended Velebit road-cycling climbs (names, gradients) for the cyclist page - not researched here.
Owner preference: any personal favourite konobas/restaurants to feature (none added due to lack of documentation).
Degarra winery opening hours conflict: the official site says Mo-Sa 11:00-22:00, but OSM says Mo-Fr 08:00-16:00.

verification.method: All 88 coordinates were compared with their cited OSM elements via the OSM API (api.openstreetmap.org; Overpass was unreachable). All 88 were reverse-geocoded with Nominatim to check the town and land/sea placement. 11 non-OSM or ambiguous items were forward-geocoded with Nominatim and Wikidata. 75 website and source URLs were checked with curl (all 200 except 5 bot-blocking 403s and the malformed camping.info URL). About 20 high-risk claims were checked against official sites. Straight-line distances were recomputed with the haversine formula.
